decisionGate.question: The Spec finding is sustained: the scripted revise/pass/pass test proves only transport, while the pre-change active model already revised the historical refusal and later provider calls are nondeterministic observations that cannot prove the new prompt prose caused decisions. The current seam has only free-text packet plus blocker `{cause,evidence}`, so no typed fact links `prerequisite_unmet` to a packet-declared prerequisite. Which contract should own durable proof?
options: Reopen the interface narrowly: preserve the two-cause enum, give packet-declared prerequisites stable typed IDs, require each `prerequisite_unmet` blocker to reference one, and validate that reference at runtime. Keep prose evidence for current absence/unlawfulness and the auditor for semantic truthfulness. Test the typed packet-to-receipt invariant and production lifecycle; do not claim deterministic model judgment.

Uphold `{cause,evidence}` and amend the follow-up authority: provider-backed sessions are dated observations only, not durable causal regressions or deterministic enforcement. Accept that prospective semantics remain nondeterministic auditor policy and drop the impossible requirement to prove that prompt prose causes revise/pass.
